clue.text: Exponent of gamesmanship playing snooker?

definitions.meaning: Stephen ... wrote the humorous book Gamesmanship, so he is its best-known exponent
to pot balls is the aim at snooker, so one who pots is at play

explanation.surface: A question about whether a snooker player is a master of underhand tactics.
explanation.walkthrough: Stephen Potter's 1947 book 'Gamesmanship' coined the term for winning by psychological ploys; snooker is a cue sport where balls are sunk into pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: The author Stephen Potter popularised gamesmanship, and a player sinking balls at snooker is one sense of the noun.

clue.text: Pass on shore a precious stone

parts.note: to shore up is to prop
an agate is a semi-precious banded stone

explanation.surface: Walking along a beach past a gem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shore' looks like the beach; it is the verb meaning support.
explanation.definitionFit: To spread or hand down, as ideas or plants, is to pass them on.

clue.text: Start to interest one's aunt somehow in the country

indicators.note: the pooled letters are put together in some other order
the first letter of the word interest is taken

parts.note: one is I, and 's adds S
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something sparks an aunt's interest in a foreign land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' shuffles I (start of 'interest'), IS and AUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: A North African state on the Mediterranean is the country meant.

clue.text: Unnecessarily detailed design of sewer's working

definitions.text: Unnecessarily detailed design of sewer's working

parts.words: Unnecessarily detailed design of sewer's working
parts.note: needlework by a seamstress is decorative stitching, and figuratively the word means embellishing a story

explanation.surface: Criticism of an overly elaborate plan for a drain system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewer' tempts as a drain; it is one who sews.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorative needlework, and figuratively exaggerated embellishment of a tale.

clue.text: Publicist discovered to be in very low state

parts.note: a PRO is a public relations officer, someone paid to publicise
something discovered has been found

explanation.surface: A press agent is found to be deeply depressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Profound describes a very deep condition, as of sleep or gloom, the depth sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Talk of past crimes in Egyptian capital perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests these letters could be ordered differently

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: capital means the first letter of the word Egyptian

explanation.surface: Discussion of past offences in Cairo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egyptian capital' looks like Cairo; it is just the letter E, rearranged with CRIMES IN by 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall and recount old memories is to talk of the past.

clue.text: That's your lot!

parts.note: the phrase sounds like 'no more for you', but lot also means one's destiny

explanation.surface: Someone ending a handout.
explanation.definitionFit: One's lot in life is one's destiny.

clue.text: University rag held by Hon Member causes offence

indicators.note: the rag word is held inside the member's letters

parts.note: MBE is a Member of the Order of the British Empire, an honour

explanation.surface: A student charity stunt hosted by an honoured person causes upset.
explanation.walkthrough: MBE is a British honour; 'rag' is a student charity event. 'causes' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To take umbrage is to take offence, so the noun means resentment.

clue.text: Night-vision?

parts.note: not optical equipment but what one sees while asleep

explanation.surface: A question about seeing in the dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Images seen during sleep are a vision at night.

clue.text: How Eleonora was wont to change her name

indicators.note: her surname changes by moving its first letter round to the end

parts.note: Eleonora Duse was a celebrated Italian actress

explanation.surface: How an actress was accustomed to alter her name.
explanation.walkthrough: Eleonora Duse (1858-1924) was a famous Italian actress; 'to change' sends the D of DUSE from front to back.
explanation.definitionFit: Was accustomed to do something means used to do it.

clue.text: Everyman edition?

parts.note: Latin for 'for all' names a volume collecting many works, an edition for every man; also a bus that carries everyone

explanation.surface: A query about a volume in the Everyman's Library series.
explanation.walkthrough: Everyman's Library is a British series of classic reprints, which makes the clue look like a publishing question; the Latin root means 'for everyone'.
explanation.definitionFit: A collected volume of several works is so called from Latin meaning 'for all', fitting a book for every reader.

clue.text: Label in slipper means it can be changed

indicators.note: the label word is placed inside the slipper word

parts.note: a mule is a backless slipper
a tab is a small label or tag

explanation.surface: A tag sewn inside a slipper shows it is alterable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something capable of alteration is described by this adjective, a synonym of changeable.

clue.text: Cutting new disc — bang on!

indicators.note: a new version of these words is made by rearranging their letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A DJ praises the freshly cut record as exactly right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' looks like recording a disc; it is the definition, as in cutting school. 'new' rearranges DISC BANGON.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting classes or duties means running off secretly, slipping away without leave.

clue.text: Friend getting married this Sunday

parts.note: a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A friend is getting married this coming Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sunday before Easter is named after the fronds strewn before Christ, so the word fills the blank before Sunday.

clue.text: Insect fastening onto jumper!

parts.note: a frog is an ornamental coat fastening
a hopper is one that jumps

explanation.surface: A button sewn on to a sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' tempts as a British sweater; it means one who jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A small jumping bug that sucks plant sap, also called a spittlebug.

clue.text: Give up — it's a curse to put on!

parts.note: a ban is an old word for a curse or anathema
to don clothes is to put them on

explanation.surface: Someone advises quitting, as a hex is a thing to place on another.
explanation.definitionFit: To relinquish or desert something is to give it up.

clue.text: A modern English home in New South Wales

parts.note: modern means new
an Englishman's home is his castle, as the proverb says

explanation.surface: A new English house built in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: Newcastle is a port city in New South Wales, Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in that Australian state bears this name.

clue.text: What mullein by another name became

definitions.text: What mullein by another name became

parts.words: What mullein by another name became
parts.note: mullein is also called Aaron's rod, and in Exodus Aaron's rod was cast down and turned into a snake

explanation.surface: A botanical riddle about what a plant turned into under a different name.
explanation.walkthrough: Mullein is a tall weed whose folk name is Aaron's rod; Exodus 7 tells of Aaron's rod turning into a snake before Pharaoh.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, Aaron's rod, the folk name for mullein, changed into a snake.

clue.text: Roosevelt in the buff, say! Pooh!

parts.note: Teddy was the nickname of President Theodore Roosevelt

indicators.note: say signals the word is spoken and heard as another

parts.note: in the buff means naked or bare

explanation.surface: An exclamation of disgust at a naked president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pooh!' looks like scorn; it is Winnie-the-Pooh, a toy. The toy was named after Roosevelt.
explanation.definitionFit: Winnie-the-Pooh is a stuffed toy, the famous example.

clue.text: Feature a Cockney's version of 21, say

indicators.note: a Cockney drops the initial H and the result is said aloud, signalled also by say

parts.note: the answer to 21 means a highbrow, said by a Cockney without its first letter

explanation.surface: How a Londoner would pronounce another word in this puzzle, given as a facial feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 across (an intellectual) is HIGHBROW; Cockney speech drops the H, giving 'ighbrow, and 'say' marks that it is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: The arch of hair above the eye is one feature of the face.

clue.text: This band's among the last I conducted

indicators.note: the answer lies among the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A conductor talks of an orchestra he last led.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretchy loop of rubber is a band of this kind.

clue.text: Urge ambassador to notice intellectual

parts.note: to egg on is to urge
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador
an ad is a notice in a newspaper

explanation.surface: An envoy is pressed to pay attention to a clever person.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookish, cerebral person is called this, an informal word for a highbrow.

clue.text: It's up to me, I've concluded, to be moving

indicators.note: the word I've is placed at the end
in a down clue the words to me are read upwards

explanation.surface: Someone decides they must act.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirring the feelings is what an affecting, touching speech does.

clue.text: Fish for tea daily?

definitions.meaning: a fish of the trout family
a daily, a cleaning woman who comes in each day, is a charwoman

explanation.surface: Asking what fish to eat at the daily evening meal.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'tea' can mean the evening meal and a 'daily' is a cleaner who comes each day.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a trout-like fish, slang for a cuppa, and a cleaning lady, three separate senses.

clue.text: Such a saucy prank!

definitions.meaning: the bud of a shrub pickled for sauce

explanation.surface: Exclaiming at a cheeky practical joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a pickled bud used in sauce and a frolicsome escapade.

clue.text: Epicurean science key to Galileo's work?

parts.note: G is a musical key
Galileo studied the heavens, the science of stars and planets

explanation.surface: A gourmet's discipline is said to unlock what Galileo did.
explanation.definitionFit: The art and science of good eating is what an epicure studies.

clue.text: Instant credit?

definitions.meaning: a moment, as in 'just a moment'
buying on credit is informally buying on this

explanation.surface: Asking about immediate loans.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a moment and also deferred payment, as in on the slate.

clue.text: This mole's said to be a man of title

indicators.note: said signals the word is heard rather than spelled

parts.note: a peer is a nobleman with a title

explanation.surface: A burrowing animal claims to be a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mole' tempts as the animal; it is a breakwater or jetty.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a stone breakwater or jetty, a structure jutting into the sea.

clue.text: A trip to arrange for country-lover

indicators.note: the letters of these words are arranged in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone organises an excursion for a lover of the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country-lover' suggests a rambler; it means one who loves their nation.
explanation.definitionFit: One who loves and loyally supports their nation is so called.

clue.text: A sudden fancy for a piece of music

definitions.meaning: a lively free-form composition, also called a capriccio

explanation.surface: Someone takes an impulsive liking to a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a whim and a light, free-form musical composition.

clue.text: Log about to be returned to judge

parts.note: to log is to record

indicators.note: the word for about is turned back to front

parts.note: RE means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A ship's log is sent back to a judge for review.
explanation.walkthrough: In England a recorder is a part-time judge in the Crown Court.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrister sitting as a part-time Crown Court judge holds this title.

clue.text: Falling behind in this

parts.note: someone behind with payments is said to be in a state of debt left unpaid

explanation.surface: A remark about lagging behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Being behind with money owed is to be in this, usually in the plural, describing overdue debt.
